newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - Siemens phone unit expects sales jump.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Siemens phone unit expects sales jump.

text.p: German industrial giant Siemens AG on Friday said it expected new telecommunications businesses and emerging markets to spark a tripling of sales in its public networks group to 35 billion marks ($22.5 billion) by 2005.

"Telecommunications is the growth industry in the world, if you look at what the world is going to do with computers and mobile communications 10 years from now," public networks (PN) chief Peter Pribilla told a news conference.
New mobile phone, Internet and service businesses will grow by 20-60 percent per year, while developing phone markets in Asia and Eastern Europe would drive the boom, Pribilla said.
Profit gains should come at the same time, if PN is able to offset price declines with productivity gains, although some jobs will be lost in Germany, Pribilla said.
The unit, which provides cable, equipment and software to public phone companies, said it expected 1996/97 sales to rise by 8.5 percent to 12.8 billion marks.
Profit in the 1996/97 business year should improve over the 354 million marks pretax earnings booked in the year to September 30. A further improvement is expected in 1997/98, it added.
Last month Siemens said group profits would not improve in 1996/97, prompting its shares to fall more than 10 percent to about 72 marks.
Analysts said profit gains were less certain because of costs to develop new businesses and stiff competition for contracts in emerging countries.
"Siemens have been very successful at getting mobile phone contracts in India and Latin America but the question is what is the margin," said Hans Peter Wodniok at Credit Lyonnais.
"A lot of times you have to lower prices to get into these markets," he said.
Pribilla highlighted several new business areas where Siemens expected growth rates far above the three to four percent in its traditional cable and switching sales.

-- Sales of mobile phone networks should reach 1.2 billion marks the year and 2.5 billion by 2000, driven by contracts in Indonesia, India and other developing economies. The United States, which recently opened its market to the European GSM mobile phone standard, could also boost sales significantly.
-- Telecommunicaitons management services, which operate entire networks for phone companies, are expected to post 55 percent annual growth and sales of one billion marks by 2000.
-- Network engineering, which provides complete planning, equipment and installation of "turnkey" phone systems, should generate two billion marks in revenue by 2000, Pribilla said.

-- Access networks business, which supplies fibre-optic and other cables that link homes to phone networks and should take in 1.1 billion marks in orders this year. By 2000 sales should reach three billion marks.

-- Broadband networks provide Deutsche Telekom AG and other phone companies with high-speed asynchronous transfer mode (ATM) technology for transmitting voice, video and data. Pribilla forecast sales would grow from 75 million marks this year to one billion marks in 2000.

-- Intelligent networks, which develop specialised telecommunication services such as toll-free numbers, and an Internet solutions business are in the start-up phase. The Internet group, based in Florida, is working on technology to let people use the Internet for regular phone calls.

In Asia, Siemens networks wants to build its market share, currently 15 percent, to 20 percent by 2000. And in Eastern Europe, where market share is also 15 percent, Pribilla said the company's presence should be expanded strongly.
Siemens is the world's second largest supplier of telecommunications equipment, behind France's Alcatel and just ahead of Lucent Technologies of the U.S.
